name: agent-browser
description: Drive the user's real, already-logged-in Chrome from the terminal or any MCP-capable agent — open pages, read them, click, type, screenshot, upload files — while organizing tabs into one group per task. Use when a task needs a browser: checking internal dashboards, filling web forms, scraping pages the user can already see, or reproducing a UI bug. Works without a debug port or a separate Chrome profile, so existing logins and sessions are preserved.
---

# Agent Browser Bridge

Control the user's **real Chrome** (the window they actually use), not a headless
clone. The browser keeps its cookies, logins, extensions and password manager.

Two ways in, same engine:

- **MCP tools** (`browser_*`), for any agent that speaks MCP.
- **CLI** (`abb <tool> '[json]'`), for shells and scripts.

## Before you start

```bash
abb doctor
```

- `ok server ... extension connected` → good, continue.
- `FAIL no bridge server` → nothing is running; the MCP server normally owns the
  port, so start your agent first, or run `node bin/mcp-server.mjs` yourself.
- `FAIL server is up ... but no extension is polling` → the Chrome extension is
  not loaded, or its card needs a reload after an edit.

Never guess at a browser failure: `browser_status` / `abb status` tells you
whether the problem is the server, the extension, or the page.

## The one rule that matters: one task, one tab group

The user's Chrome is full of their own tabs. Do **not** work in whatever tab
happens to be active.

1. Start every task with `browser_group_begin { "title": "<short task name>" }`.
   Use a name a human recognizes — `"pricing research"`, `"yuque weekly report"` —
   not `"task 1"`.
2. Every later call targets that group automatically, even if the user is
   looking at a different tab.
3. `browser_tab_new` joins the group automatically.
4. Finish with `browser_group_end`. Tabs stay open so the user can review them;
   only pass `closeTabs: true` when they asked to clean up.

One session usually contains several small tasks. Open a new group per task
rather than reusing the previous group.

## Typical loop

```
browser_group_begin { title, url }
browser_snapshot          → see what is on the page (accessibility tree)
browser_click { selector }→ move + click; the on-page cursor shows the target
browser_snapshot          → confirm the page changed
browser_text              → read the result
browser_group_end
```

- `snapshot` beats `screenshot` for finding elements, and costs far fewer tokens.
- `selector` accepts a CSS selector **or** the exact visible text of an element.
- `browser_eval` is the escape hatch when no tool fits; prefer specific tools.
- For long pages, `browser_scroll { pages: 1 }` then read again.

## Visual cursor

Clicks and typing show a large glowing cursor, a highlight on the target and a
ripple, so the user can see what is happening. It is drawn inside the page only:
it does not move the system pointer, it disappears on navigation, and it stays
silent while the tab is hidden or Chrome is in the background
(`browser_visual_cursor` to change that).

## Safety

- Never type passwords, one-time codes or card numbers. Ask the user to do that
  part themselves; the browser is already logged in, so usually you do not need it.
- Ask before anything that spends money, sends a message, publishes content, or
  deletes data. A click is cheap to make and hard to take back.
- Do not navigate away from a tab that has unsaved input without saying so.
- `browser://`, `chrome://` and extension-store pages cannot be scripted.

## When something breaks

- Page looks stale → `browser_open` again, or `browser_eval { expression: "location.href" }`.
- Element not found → `browser_snapshot` and match on the visible text instead.
- Everything times out → `abb doctor`; usually the extension needs a reload after
  its files changed (`chrome://extensions` → reload arrow).
- Full guide: `docs/troubleshooting.md`.

# Agent Browser Bridge

Drive **your real Chrome** — the window you actually use, with all your logins
intact — from any local AI agent. One Chrome extension, one zero-dependency
Node bridge, and two ways to call it: MCP tools or a CLI.

No debug port. No second Chrome profile. No lost cookies.

---

## Why this exists

Every "let the agent use my browser" path breaks somewhere:

| Approach | What goes wrong |
|---|---|
| `--remote-debugging-port` on your normal profile | Chrome 136+ refuses to open the port on the default user-data-dir |
| Launch a separate debug profile | Empty browser: no logins, no extensions, no history |
| Copy your profile to a new directory | Chrome protects the profile; the copy is unreadable or takes forever |
| Headless / cloud browser | Needs re-authentication, and internal sites may not allow it |

This project takes the one path Chrome still allows: a **local extension with the
`debugger` permission**. The extension is already inside your browsing session,
so it can attach to a tab and speak the DevTools Protocol — without opening any
port and without leaving your profile.

No dependency on ChatGPT, Codex, Playwright, Puppeteer, or any cloud service.
Plain Node (>= 18) and Chrome.

---

## How it works

```
agent (MCP client or CLI)
        │  JSON-RPC over stdio        │  HTTP on 127.0.0.1:9333
        ▼                             ▼
  MCP server (node)  ──── queue ───► hub ──── long poll ───► Chrome extension
                                                                │ chrome.debugger
                                                                ▼
                                                          your live tabs
```

- **extension/** — MV3 service worker. Polls the hub, executes actions against
  tabs through `chrome.debugger` (CDP), manages tab groups, draws the cursor.
- **bin/mcp-server.mjs** — owns the hub port, exposes 21 MCP tools. If the port
  is already taken, it silently becomes a *client* of the running hub, so several
  agents can share one Chrome.
- **bin/abb.mjs** — the same operations from a shell, plus `doctor` and `selftest`.

---

## Requirements

- Node.js >= 18 (no npm packages are installed)
- Google Chrome (or any Chromium 116+ browser that supports MV3 + `debugger`)
- macOS, Linux or Windows

---

## Install

### 1. Get the code

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<you>/agent-browser-bridge.git
cd agent-browser-bridge
```

### 2. Load the extension (once per Chrome profile)

1. Open `chrome://extensions`
2. Turn on **Developer mode** (top right)
3. Click **Load unpacked** and select this repo's `extension/` folder
4. Pin the extension so you can see it

Chrome does **not** auto-reload unpacked extensions. After any edit inside
`extension/`, click the reload arrow on its card.

> The extension shows a "…is debugging this browser" bar while attached. That is
> normal and disappears when the agent stops using the tab.

### 3. Connect your agent

**Option A — MCP (recommended).** Point your agent at the server:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agent-browser": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/agent-browser-bridge/bin/mcp-server.mjs"],
      "env": { "ABB_CLIENT_ID": "claude" }
    }
  }
}
```

- **Claude Code**: `claude mcp add agent-browser -- node /abs/path/bin/mcp-server.mjs`
- **Cursor / Windsurf**: paste the JSON above into the MCP settings file
  (`.cursor/mcp.json` or the app's MCP panel)
- **Qoder** and other GUI clients: add a stdio connector with the same
  command/args (see `docs/tools.md` for a per-client table)
- **Any other MCP client**: the server speaks standard MCP over stdio

**Option B — CLI only.** No MCP client needed:

```bash
node bin/abb.mjs doctor          # is everything wired up?
node bin/abb.mjs selftest        # end-to-end check against your Chrome
node bin/abb.mjs group_begin '{"title":"research","url":"https://example.com"}'
node bin/abb.mjs text '{"limit":3000}'
node bin/abb.mjs group_end
```

Add `alias abb="node /abs/path/bin/abb.mjs"` to your shell rc to shorten that.

### 4. Verify

```bash
node bin/abb.mjs selftest
```

It starts a tiny local page, then exercises handshake, task group, read, click,
type, accessibility snapshot, screenshot and cleanup. All checks should pass.

---

## The usage rule: one task, one tab group

The bridge is designed around a habit that keeps the user's browser sane:

- `browser_group_begin { title }` — start each task in its own named group
- every later call targets that group, even if the user switched tabs
- `browser_group_end` — finish; tabs stay open for review

This is also what makes multi-agent use safe: each agent keeps its own pointer
(`ABB_CLIENT_ID`), so two agents never steal each other's tabs.

---

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `browser_status` | Bridge + extension health, versions |
| `browser_group_begin` / `browser_group_end` / `browser_groups` | Task groups |
| `browser_tabs` / `browser_tab_new` / `browser_tab_select` / `browser_tab_close` | Tabs |
| `browser_open` | Navigate the task tab |
| `browser_text` / `browser_html` | Read the page |
| `browser_snapshot` | Accessibility tree (best for finding elements) |
| `browser_screenshot` | PNG of the tab |
| `browser_click` / `browser_type` / `browser_press_key` | Interact |
| `browser_wait_for` / `browser_scroll` | Timing and long pages |
| `browser_upload` | Set files on a file input |
| `browser_eval` | Run JS in the page (escape hatch) |
| `browser_visual_cursor` | Toggle the on-page cursor |

Full schemas and examples: [docs/tools.md](docs/tools.md).

---

## The visual cursor

Clicks and typing draw a large glowing pointer, highlight the target element and
play a ripple, so a human watching can follow along. It is an overlay inside the
page:

- does not move the system pointer
- `pointer-events: none`, so it never blocks a click
- disappears on navigation (re-injected on the next action)
- silent while the tab is hidden or Chrome is in the background
  (`browser_visual_cursor { backgroundSilent: false }` to always show it)
- not available on `chrome://` pages

---

## Security model

- Everything runs on `127.0.0.1`. Nothing is sent anywhere.
- The extension has `debugger` + `tabs` + `tabGroups` + `storage`; it can read any
  page you have open. Treat it like giving an agent your browser session.
- There is no authentication on the local port: any local process can submit
  commands while the bridge runs. On shared machines, stop the MCP server when
  you are not using it.
- The agent should never type passwords or one-time codes. Log in yourself; the
  bridge reuses the session.

---

## Limitations

- Unpacked extension = one manual "Load unpacked" per Chrome profile, and a
  manual reload after editing extension files.
- `chrome://`, the Chrome Web Store and other protected pages cannot be scripted.
- Iframes are reachable only through `browser_eval`, not through `browser_click`.
- Chrome must be running with a window open; the extension cannot drive a closed
  browser (start Chrome first).
- One Chrome window can be driven by several agents, but each agent works in its
  own tab group; two agents editing the *same* form will conflict.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `extension is not connected` | Load `extension/` at `chrome://extensions`, then reload the card |
| `unknown action: hello` | The extension on disk is newer than the loaded one — click reload |
| `element not found` | Use `browser_snapshot`, then match on visible text |
| Everything times out | `abb doctor`; check the port matches the extension's options page |
| Port already in use | Another agent owns the hub. That is fine — this one becomes a client |

More: [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md).

---

## Development

```bash
node --check bin/mcp-server.mjs     # syntax
node bin/abb.mjs doctor             # environment
node bin/abb.mjs selftest           # end-to-end against live Chrome
node test/mcp-smoke.mjs             # protocol test with two independent agents
ABB_PORT=9444 node bin/abb.mjs status   # use a different port
```

Layout:

```
bin/         mcp-server.mjs (MCP stdio), abb.mjs (CLI)
lib/         hub.mjs (HTTP + queue), client.mjs, tools.mjs
extension/   manifest.json, sw.js, options.html/js
docs/        architecture, tools, troubleshooting
SKILL.md     agent-skill entry point
```

See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for the protocol details.

---

# Agent Browser Bridge（中文说明）

让本地任意 AI Agent 操作**你正在用的那个 Chrome**——带着你所有的登录状态、扩展和
历史记录，而不是另开一个空白浏览器。

一个 Chrome 扩展 + 一个零依赖的 Node 服务，两种调用方式：MCP 工具，或者命令行。

不需要调试端口，不需要第二个浏览器配置，不会丢登录态。

---

## 为什么要做这个

"让 Agent 用我的浏览器"这件事，常见做法各有一个硬伤：

| 做法 | 卡在哪 |
|---|---|
| 给日常 Chrome 加 `--remote-debugging-port` | Chrome 136 以后，默认配置目录直接不开调试端口 |
| 另开一个调试用的 Chrome | 空白浏览器：没有登录态、没有扩展、没有历史 |
| 把日常配置目录复制一份 | Chrome 会保护这个目录，复制出来的数据读不了，或者慢到不可用 |
| 无头浏览器 / 云端浏览器 | 要重新登录，内网站点还可能直接拒绝 |

本项目走的是 Chrome 仍然允许的那条路：**一个带 `debugger` 权限的本地扩展**。
扩展本身就在你的浏览会话里，所以它可以挂到某个标签页上、使用浏览器的调试协议——
既不用开端口，也不离开你的配置。

不依赖 ChatGPT、Codex、Playwright、Puppeteer，也不依赖任何云服务。
只要 Node 18+ 和 Chrome。

---

## 它是怎么工作的

```
Agent（MCP 客户端 或 命令行）
        │  stdio 上的 JSON-RPC        │  127.0.0.1:9333 上的 HTTP
        ▼                             ▼
   MCP 服务（Node）  ──── 队列 ───► 中转服务 hub ──── 长轮询 ────► Chrome 扩展
                                                                    │ chrome.debugger
                                                                    ▼
                                                              你正在用的标签页
```

- **extension/**：Chrome 扩展的后台脚本（MV3）。它向中转服务轮询命令，用
  `chrome.debugger` 执行（底层就是浏览器的调试协议），同时负责标签组和屏幕上的光标。
- **bin/mcp-server.mjs**：占据本地端口，对外提供 21 个 MCP 工具。如果端口已经被
  别的实例占着，它不会报错，而是自动降级成"客户端"，把命令转发过去——所以多个
  Agent 可以同时用同一个 Chrome。
- **bin/abb.mjs**：同样的能力，从命令行调，另外附带体检和自测。

---

## 环境要求

- Node.js 18 或更高（不安装任何 npm 包）
- Chrome（或任何支持 MV3 + `debugger` 的 Chromium 116+ 浏览器）
- macOS / Linux / Windows 都可以

---

## 安装

### 第一步：拿到代码

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<you>/agent-browser-bridge.git
cd agent-browser-bridge
```

### 第二步：加载扩展（每个 Chrome 配置只需一次）

1. 打开 `chrome://extensions`
2. 右上角打开**开发者模式**
3. 点**加载已解压的扩展程序**，选中本仓库的 `extension/` 目录
4. 建议把扩展图标固定到工具栏，方便看状态

Chrome **不会**自动重载未打包的扩展。以后只要改过 `extension/` 里的文件，就要回到
扩展页点一下卡片上的刷新箭头。

> 扩展工作期间，标签页上方会出现"正在调试此浏览器"的提示条。这是正常现象，
> Agent 停止操作后就会消失。

### 第三步：接上你的 Agent

**方式 A：MCP（推荐）**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agent-browser": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/绝对路径/agent-browser-bridge/bin/mcp-server.mjs"],
      "env": { "ABB_CLIENT_ID": "claude" }
    }
  }
}
```

- **Claude Code**: `claude mcp add agent-browser -- node /绝对路径/bin/mcp-server.mjs`
- **Cursor / Windsurf**：把上面的 JSON 贴进 MCP 设置文件（`.cursor/mcp.json` 或应用里的 MCP 面板）
- **Qoder 等图形客户端**：添加一个 stdio 连接器，命令和参数同上
- **其他 MCP 客户端**：服务端讲的是标准 MCP，照常配置即可

**方式 B：只用命令行**

```bash
node bin/abb.mjs doctor          # 检查环境
node bin/abb.mjs selftest        # 对着你的 Chrome 跑一遍端到端自测
node bin/abb.mjs group_begin '{"title":"查资料","url":"https://example.com"}'
node bin/abb.mjs text '{"limit":3000}'
node bin/abb.mjs group_end
```

想少打字可以在 shell 配置里加一行：
`alias abb="node /绝对路径/bin/abb.mjs"`。

### 第四步：验收

```bash
node bin/abb.mjs selftest
```

它会自己起一个很小的本地页面，然后依次验证：握手、建任务组、读页面、点击、输入、
无障碍快照、截图、清理。全部通过才算装好。

---

## 使用规矩：一个任务，一个标签组

桥接是围绕一个习惯设计的：

- `browser_group_begin { title }`：每开始一个任务，建一个以任务名命名的标签组
- 之后所有操作都只作用于这个组，哪怕你切去看别的标签
- `browser_group_end`：收尾，标签保留，方便你自己回看

这也是多 Agent 共存的关键：每个 Agent 记自己的"当前组"（用 `ABB_CLIENT_ID` 区分），
互不抢标签。

---

## 工具一览

| 工具 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `browser_status` | 桥接与扩展的健康状态、版本 |
| `browser_group_begin` / `browser_group_end` / `browser_groups` | 任务标签组 |
| `browser_tabs` / `browser_tab_new` / `browser_tab_select` / `browser_tab_close` | 标签页 |
| `browser_open` | 让任务标签跳转到某个网址 |
| `browser_text` / `browser_html` | 读页面内容 |
| `browser_snapshot` | 无障碍树（找元素最好用） |
| `browser_screenshot` | 标签页截图 |
| `browser_click` / `browser_type` / `browser_press_key` | 交互 |
| `browser_wait_for` / `browser_scroll` | 等待与滚动 |
| `browser_upload` | 给文件输入框塞文件 |
| `browser_eval` | 在页面里跑 JavaScript（兜底手段） |
| `browser_visual_cursor` | 开关屏幕上的光标 |

完整参数和示例见 [docs/tools.md](docs/tools.md)。

---

## 屏幕上的光标

点击和输入时，页面里会出现一个放大的发光指针，目标元素被描边高亮，点击时有一圈涟漪。
这是画在页面里的一层覆盖物：

- 不会移动系统鼠标指针
- 设了 `pointer-events: none`，永远不会挡住页面点击
- 页面跳转后自动消失，下次操作重新出现
- 标签在后台、或 Chrome 不在前台时不显示（想让它一直显示，把
  `browser_visual_cursor` 的 `backgroundSilent` 设为 false）
- `chrome://` 开头的页面画不了

---

## 安全说明

- 所有通信都在 `127.0.0.1`，不会往外发任何数据。
- 扩展拥有 `debugger`、`tabs`、`tabGroups`、`storage` 权限，能读取你打开的任何网页。
  把它理解成"你把浏览器会话交给了这个 Agent"。
- 本地端口没有鉴权：桥接运行期间，本机任何进程都能提交命令。共用电脑时，用完建议
  停掉 MCP 服务。
- Agent 不应该替你输入密码或验证码。你自己登录，桥接直接复用已有会话。

---

## 已知限制

- 未打包扩展意味着：每个 Chrome 配置要手动加载一次；改扩展代码后要手动点刷新。
- `chrome://`、Chrome 应用商店等受保护页面无法脚本化。
- 跨域 iframe 里的元素只能通过 `browser_eval` 操作，`browser_click` 够不到。
- Chrome 必须开着且有窗口；扩展没法驱动一个没启动的浏览器。
- 多个 Agent 可以共用同一个 Chrome，但各自在自己的标签组里工作；两个 Agent 同时改
  同一个表单会互相覆盖。

---

## 排障

| 现象 | 处理 |
|---|---|
| `extension is not connected` | 在 `chrome://extensions` 加载 `extension/`，然后刷新扩展卡片 |
| `unknown action: hello` | 磁盘上的扩展比已加载的新，点卡片上的刷新箭头 |
| `element not found` | 先 `browser_snapshot`，再用可见文字去匹配 |
| 全部超时 | 跑 `abb doctor`；确认端口和扩展选项页里的一致 |
| 端口被占用 | 已有别的 Agent 占着中转服务，这是正常的——本实例会自动变成客户端 |

更多见 [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md)。

---

```bash
node --check bin/mcp-server.mjs          # 语法检查

```

目录结构：


# Architecture

## Pieces

| Piece | File | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Extension | `extension/sw.js` | Runs inside Chrome. Polls for commands, drives tabs via `chrome.debugger`, manages tab groups, draws the cursor. |
| Hub | `lib/hub.mjs` | Owns the local HTTP port. Queues commands, holds the extension's long poll, delivers results. |
| MCP server | `bin/mcp-server.mjs` | Speaks MCP over stdio. Owns a hub, or becomes a client if the port is taken. |
| CLI | `bin/abb.mjs` | Same operations from a shell; `doctor` and `selftest` live here. |
| Tools | `lib/tools.mjs` | Tool schemas shared by both entry points. |

## Why an extension and not CDP

Chrome 136 and later ignore `--remote-debugging-port` when the profile is the
default one, and refuse to open a debug socket on a profile that is already in
use. Copying the profile is blocked by the OS keychain/attribute protections.

An extension with the `debugger` permission is the remaining supported path: it
already lives inside the browsing session, so `chrome.debugger.attach(tabId)`
works without any port, and the profile never changes.

The trade-off: the extension can only see tabs, not browser chrome, and it must
be loaded unpacked (once per profile) because this is not published to the store.

## Wire protocol

The transport is plain HTTP on `127.0.0.1` (default port 9333), with four routes:

| Route | Direction | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /poll` | extension → hub | Long poll held up to 25 s. Returns `{id, action, args}` or `204`. |
| `POST /result` | extension → hub | `{id, ok, result | error}` for a previously delivered command. |
| `POST /call` | CLI / MCP client → hub | `{action, args}` → `{ok, result | error}`. Synchronous. |
| `GET /status` | anyone | `{connected, lastPollAgoMs, queued, pending, port}`. |

Long polling keeps the MV3 service worker alive (a pending `fetch` counts as
activity, and the alarm re-arms every 30 s as a backstop). Commands are delivered
one at a time; the hub keeps a FIFO queue and a 60 s timeout per command.

### Why not WebSocket

A `fetch`-based long poll survives service-worker suspension better than an
`EventSource`/WebSocket that Chrome may tear down, and it needs no extra runtime
in Node. The cost is up to one round trip of latency after idle, which is
irrelevant for UI automation.

## Actions

Actions are plain strings handled by a `switch` in `extension/sw.js`:
`tabs, open, text, html, snapshot, screenshot, click, type, press_key, wait_for,
scroll, eval, upload, tab_new, tab_select, tab_close, group_begin, group_end,
groups, visual_cursor, hello, ping`.

`click` and `type` resolve a target with:

1. `document.querySelector(selector)`
2. fallback: exact match on the trimmed `innerText` of
   `a, button, input, [role=button], [role=tab], li, div, span`

That fallback is why an agent can pass visible text (`"Sign in"`) instead of a
brittle CSS path.

## Task groups and clients

Each caller sends `clientId` with every command (from `ABB_CLIENT_ID`, default
`default`). The extension keeps:

```jsonc
{ "clients": { "claude": { "groupId": 123, "tabId": 456, "groupTitle": "..." } } }
```

`currentTab(clientId)` resolves in this order:

1. the remembered tab, if it still exists and is in the remembered group
2. the active tab of that group
3. the last tab of that group
4. the browser's active tab (no task group)

This is what makes "operations follow the task, not the user's current tab"
work — and why two agents can share one Chrome without fighting.

## Multi-agent: hub vs client

Only one process can bind the port. `bin/mcp-server.mjs` tries `listen()`; on
`EADDRINUSE` it switches to client mode and forwards every call to
`POST /call`. The CLI always talks HTTP, so it works in both cases.

```
agent A ── stdio ── mcp-server (hub, owns :9333) ─┐
agent B ── stdio ── mcp-server (client) ──────────┤──► extension
shell   ─────────── abb (client) ─────────────────┘
```

The extension is the only browser-facing process, so no matter how many agents
connect, only one debugger session per tab exists.

## Debugger lifecycle

`ensureAttached(tabId)` attaches with protocol 1.3 and detaches the previous tab,
so at most one tab is being driven at a time. Chrome shows its "being debugged"
infobar for the attached tab; it disappears after detach or navigation.

Screenshots use `Page.captureScreenshot`; the accessibility tree uses
`Accessibility.getFullAXTree` and is flattened into one line per node.

## Visual cursor

`CURSOR_INSTALL` is an idempotent script evaluated in the page: it creates a
fixed-position container with an SVG arrow, a ripple ring and a label chip, all
`pointer-events: none`. Because it is `position: fixed`, any page scroll between
"move the cursor" and "click" would shift the page under it — so `click` and
`type` scroll, measure, act and re-measure inside a single evaluation.

Injection is skipped when `document.visibilityState !== 'visible'`, or when
`document.hasFocus()` is false while `backgroundSilent` is on. Protected pages
(`chrome://`, the Web Store) reject injection; actions still run there, just
without the overlay.

# Tool reference

Every tool exists in two forms: `browser_<name>` (MCP) and `<name>` (CLI, via
`abb <name> '{"json"}'`). Arguments are JSON objects.

| Tool | Arguments | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `browser_status` | – | hub status + extension version |
| `browser_group_begin` | `title` (required), `color?`, `url?` | `{groupId, tabId, title, color, url}` |
| `browser_group_end` | `closeTabs?`, `groupId?` | `{groupId, closedTabs}` |
| `browser_groups` | – | list of `{groupId, title, color, tabCount, taskGroup}` |
| `browser_tabs` | `groupOnly?` | list of `{index, id, active, groupId, groupTitle, taskGroup, url, title}` |
| `browser_tab_new` | `url?` | `{id, url, title, groupId}` |
| `browser_tab_select` | `id?` or `index?` | `"active: <url>"` |
| `browser_tab_close` | `id?` or `index?` | `"closed"` |
| `browser_open` | `url` | `{url, title}` |
| `browser_text` | `limit?` (6000) | page text |
| `browser_html` | `limit?` (20000) | page HTML |
| `browser_snapshot` | – | accessibility tree as text |
| `browser_screenshot` | `fullPage?` | PNG (base64) |
| `browser_click` | `selector`, `label?` | `"CLICKED:<text>"` |
| `browser_type` | `selector`, `text`, `label?` | `"TYPED"` |
| `browser_press_key` | `key` | `"pressed <key>"` |
| `browser_wait_for` | `selector`, `timeoutMs?` (15000) | `"found <selector>"` |
| `browser_scroll` | `pages?` (1, negative = up) | `"scrolled N page(s)"` |
| `browser_eval` | `expression` | value (strings as-is, objects JSON) |
| `browser_upload` | `selector`, `filePath` | `"uploaded <path>"` |
| `browser_visual_cursor` | `enabled?`, `backgroundSilent?` | `{enabled, backgroundSilent}` |

## `selector` rules

1. Tried as a CSS selector first: `#submit`, `button[type=submit]`, `.card a`.
2. If nothing matches, the exact trimmed visible text is matched against
   `a, button, input, [role=button], [role=tab], li, div, span`:
   `"Sign in"`, `"下一页"`.

Prefer a stable CSS selector when one exists; the text fallback is a convenience
for pages with generated class names.

## Examples

```bash
# start a task
abb group_begin '{"title":"invoice lookup","url":"https://example.com/app"}'

# look around
abb snapshot
abb text '{"limit":2000}'

# interact
abb click '{"selector":"#search","label":"focus search"}'
abb type '{"selector":"#search","text":"INV-2026-0042"}'
abb press_key '{"key":"Enter"}'          # or: abb click '{"selector":"Search"}'
abb wait_for '{"selector":".result-row","timeoutMs":8000}'

# capture
abb screenshot '{"fullPage":true}'        # prints { image: "[base64 png, N chars]" }

# finish
abb group_end
```

MCP equivalent of a click:

```json
{ "name": "browser_click",
  "arguments": { "selector": "#search", "label": "focus search" } }
```

## Behavior notes

- `browser_open` and `browser_tab_new` wait for the load event (up to 30 s).
- `browser_click` moves the on-page cursor, highlights the target, waits ~0.4 s,
  then clicks, so a human can follow. Set `browser_visual_cursor {enabled:false}`
  to make it instant.
- `browser_type` sets `.value` and dispatches `input` + `change`. It does **not**
  simulate per-character typing; frameworks that need real key events can be
  driven with `browser_press_key` or `browser_eval`.
- `browser_eval` runs in the page's main world. Use it for iframes, shadow DOM
  and custom events.
- Screenshots come back as base64 in the MCP image content block.

## Registering the MCP server

| Client | Where |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude mcp add agent-browser -- node /abs/bin/mcp-server.mjs` |
| Cursor | `.cursor/mcp.json` → `mcpServers` entry |
| Windsurf | MCP panel → add stdio server |
| Qoder | Settings → MCP / Connectors → add stdio server |
| Generic | any client supporting MCP over stdio |

Config shape:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agent-browser": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/abs/path/bin/mcp-server.mjs"],
      "env": { "ABB_CLIENT_ID": "claude", "ABB_PORT": "9333" }
    }
  }
}
```

Give each agent its own `ABB_CLIENT_ID`: the task-group pointer is stored per
client, so two agents will not steal each other's tabs.

# Troubleshooting

Start here:

```bash
node bin/abb.mjs doctor
```

It checks Node, whether the hub is listening, whether the extension is polling,
and prints the extension path to load.

## `extension is not connected`

The server is up but nothing is polling it.

1. `chrome://extensions` → is **Agent Browser Bridge** listed and enabled?
2. If not: Developer mode → Load unpacked → select `extension/`.
3. If yes: click the reload arrow on its card (Chrome does not auto-reload
   unpacked extensions after files change).
4. Still failing? Open the extension's **service worker** console (click
   "service worker" on its card) and check for errors. A syntax error in
   `sw.js` stops the poll loop entirely.
5. Port mismatch: the extension polls whatever is in its options page (default
   9333). If you set `ABB_PORT`, open the extension options and match it.

## `unknown action: hello`

The extension on disk is newer than the one Chrome has loaded. Click the reload
arrow on the extension card. `hello` is the version handshake — a bridge that
cannot answer it is out of date.

## `element not found: <selector>`

- The page may still be loading: `browser_wait_for { selector }` first.
- The element may be inside an iframe: `browser_click` cannot reach it. Use
  `browser_eval` with `document.querySelector('iframe').contentDocument`.
- The selector may match visually identical elements: use `browser_snapshot`
  and click by exact visible text instead.
- Content may be lazy-loaded: `browser_scroll { pages: 1 }` then retry.

## Clicks do nothing

Some apps only react to trusted events or need a real focus change.

- Try clicking a parent element (`.card` instead of `.card span`).
- Try `browser_eval { expression: "document.querySelector('#x').click()" }`.
- For React/Vue inputs, `browser_type` sets the value with `input` + `change`
  events; if the framework ignores that, follow with
  `browser_press_key { key: "Tab" }` or send a real keystroke after focusing.

## Everything times out

- `abb doctor` — usually the extension is disconnected.
- `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9333/status` — is the hub alive?
- If the status shows `connected: false`, the extension side is the problem.
- If the hub is not listening at all, the agent that owns it exited. Start the
  MCP server (or your agent) again.

## Port already in use

Not an error. The first process owns the hub; every later MCP server becomes a
client and forwards to it. If you *want* a separate bridge (for example a second
Chrome profile), give it a different port:

```bash
ABB_PORT=9444 node bin/mcp-server.mjs
```

and set the same port in that profile's extension options page.

## The "being debugged" bar stays

The extension detaches when another tab is targeted or when the browser closes
the debugging session. If it lingers, reload the extension; the session is
cleared. It never affects the page itself.

## Cursor does not appear

Expected in these cases:

- the tab is hidden or Chrome is in the background (`backgroundSilent` is on)
- the page is `chrome://`, the Web Store, or a PDF viewer
- `browser_visual_cursor { enabled: false }` was set

Turn it back on with `browser_visual_cursor { enabled: true, backgroundSilent: false }`.

## Login pages

Do not have the agent type credentials. Log in manually in Chrome once; the
bridge reuses that session. If a site forces a fresh login, ask the user to do it
in the tab the agent opened.

## Collecting a useful bug report

```bash
node bin/abb.mjs doctor
node bin/abb.mjs status
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9333/status
```

Plus the extension's service-worker console output and the exact tool call that
failed. That usually identifies the failing layer in one pass.
